references.text: The Lord's Spirit came upon Othniel, just as it later came upon other judges and leaders in Israel, giving them power to do God's will.
Joshua was filled with the spirit of wisdom when Moses laid his hands on him, an early example of God's Spirit equipping leaders.
The Lord's Spirit came upon Gideon in a similar way, giving him strength to lead Israel against their enemies.
The Lord's Spirit came upon Jephthah, and he went out to fight the Ammonites, just as Othniel went out to war.
The Lord's Spirit came powerfully upon Samson, another example of how the Spirit equips judges with supernatural strength.
The Lord's Spirit came upon Saul, and he was changed into a different man, showing the same pattern of the Spirit's empowerment.
The Lord's Spirit came upon David from the day he was anointed and remained with him, just as it did with Othniel.
The prophecy about the Messiah upon whom the Lord's Spirit will rest connects the theme of the Spirit equipping leaders.
The Lord's Spirit is upon the Anointed One to proclaim freedom, fulfilling the pattern of the Spirit's empowerment.
Jesus promises that his disciples will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon them, continuing the pattern of the Spirit's empowerment for service.
